name: team_add
unavailable: The person allows one agent in this chat: there is no team. Do the work yourself.
description:
Add a subagent and start it at once, in the background, on its part of the work. Only you, the main agent, add subagents. You lead: subagents do the work while you plan, coordinate and review — once you have one, tools that change things are refused to you.

- `name` is how everyone addresses it: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, after what it owns (`parser`, `api-tests`). `role` is its position, one line: what it owns. `task` is its brief and must stand on its own — it sees nothing of this conversation: what to do, when it is done, and what to report.
- `goal` is the team's goal in a line; your first subagent needs it, and every subagent is told it.
- `lead: true` makes it a sub-manager: it directs the subagents you place under it (`parent`), reviews their reports and reports to you; it does not add or stop subagents itself.
- `mode` is its permission mode: its parent's by default, never looser. With a stricter mode you may give `request` options — kinds of action (read, write, execute) it may ask you for with team_request; you decide with team_decide.
- The person sets how many agents the team may have, you included; past that this is refused. When the model is already serving as many requests as it can at once, the subagent waits for a slot and starts when one frees.
- It reports with team_finish (or its final reply). Meanwhile team_send messages it, team_read shows the tree and the room, team_assign gives it new work, team_replace replaces it, team_stop stops it.
- Agents: {{agents}}

name.description: Its name in the team, after what it owns

role.description: Its position, one line: what it owns

goal.description: The team's goal in one line: needed with your first member; a new one is told to members added from now on

lead.description: A sub-manager: directs the subagents placed under it (default: false)

model.description: Run it on another model — only one the person named in this conversation (its id or name, as in the list in your instructions). Default: the session's model.

parent.description: The sub-manager to place it under (default: you, lead)

mode.description: Its permission mode: its parent's or stricter (default: its parent's)

request.description: With a stricter mode only: kinds of action it may ask you for (team_request)

variables.agents: the agents a member may be: `name — description`, separated by "; " (as task's)
